name: Quantizer
description: This algorithm is a multi-channel CV quantizer, loosely based on the Quad Quantizer algorithm on the disting EX. It supports microtuning (see above), but this is not a requirement. It quantizes CV inputs and generates CV outputs and/or MIDI output. The quantization parameters are common to all channels; the individual channels' parameters are solely related to routing.
use_cases: Quantizing CV inputs to musical scales
Generating MIDI output from CV signals
Creating even note patterns from LFOs using Warped mode
Constraining quantized notes to specific scales and modes
gui_description: The display has different screens depending on the current parameter and tuning. When key, scale, mode, or mask parameters are selected and 12-degree logic applies, a graphical view of one octave in piano key arrangement is shown, with bright notes indicating selected notes and darker ones deselected. Otherwise, the display shows detailed channel information: input voltage and MIDI note, sampled voltage, lookup and output quantized note numbers, and output voltage with note name/cents. If a Scala file is in use, the tuning is shown in cents or as a ratio.

parameters.name: Input transpose
parameters.description: Sets the input transposition, in 12-TET semitones.

parameters.name: Key
parameters.description: Sets the key (C, D, E, etc.).

parameters.name: Scale
parameters.description: The scale to quantize into. Defaults to Chromatic.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Sets the mode, that is, the rotation of the notes within the scale. If the selected scale is 'Major', the mode is displayed by one of the familiar names Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian, or Locrian.

parameters.name: Output transpose
parameters.description: Sets the output transposition, in 12-TET semitones.

parameters.name: Output gate mode
parameters.description: Sets the behaviour of the gate/trigger outputs. The options are: 'Triggers', 'Inv Triggers' (inverted triggers, always high except for a low pulse when the trigger is fired, useful for driving an envelope generator which is generally in sustain but which needs to be retriggered when the chord changes), and 'Gates' (in which case the output is gated by the corresponding gate input). Note that this also applies to any MIDI output.

parameters.name: Gate offset
parameters.description: Offsets (delays) the gate inputs relative to the pitch inputs. This is useful to allow pitch CVs to settle before they are sampled on the rising gate, and also to cope with modules which output both a pitch and gate but change their gate first.

parameters.name: MIDI channel (in)
parameters.description: The MIDI channel to receive on.

parameters.name: MIDI channel (out)
parameters.description: The MIDI channel to output notes on.

parameters.name: Output to breakout
parameters.description: Enables MIDI output to the breakout.

parameters.name: Output to Select Bus
parameters.description: Enables MIDI output to the Select Bus.

parameters.name: Output to internal
parameters.description: Enables internal MIDI output – that is, MIDI is sent to the other algorithms.

parameters.name: Send pitch bend
parameters.description: If enabled, a pitch bend message is sent with each note on message to adjust the note tuning according to the selected microtuning.

parameters.name: Pitch bend range
parameters.description: Sets the pitch bend range, in semitones. For the 'Send pitch bend' function to work properly, this should match the pitch bend range of the receiving synth.

output_ports.name: CV output
output_ports.description: The pitch CV output bus. Always uses 'Replace' output mode.

output_ports.name: Gate output
output_ports.description: The gate output bus, according to the 'Output gate mode' parameter. Always uses 'Replace' output mode.

output_ports.name: Change output
output_ports.description: The 'change trigger' output bus. Fires a trigger pulse when the quantized note changes. Always uses 'Replace' output mode.
